interpretation: Public-web evidence can narrow assumptions but cannot be merged into a fictional completed-order dataset. Status values distinguish partially filled fields from unresolved enterprise-internal data.

public_evidence.historical_corridor: Yangpu-Tuanjiecun ran weekly at launch in 2011, 40-48 containers per train and 55-60 hours.
public_evidence.endpoint_snapshot: In 2021 Shanghai listed Chongqing among 27 connected cities and stated that the Shanghai endpoint was Luchaogang centre station.
public_evidence.frequency_boundary: Chongqing was not among the six lines explicitly named as fixed-cycle daily services in that 2021 response.
public_evidence.current_network_context: Shanghai reported more than one million sea-rail TEU and service to over 40 cities in 2025, but did not publish a Chongqing-specific timetable.

gaps.model_treatment: Use the historical 55-60-hour band only as a labelled corridor sensitivity; do not claim a current scheduled direct train.

public_evidence.published_scope: Comparative Chongqing-Shanghai value quoted by a Minsheng Shipping operations manager; no fee decomposition.

gaps.model_treatment: Apply to the rail leg and add drayage explicitly, while warning that this may double-count if the historical quote was all-in.
Use CNY 200 and one hour as transparent sensitivity inputs; keep scheduled waiting as 1/4/8-hour assumptions and never net policy support from customer price.

public_evidence.official_reliability_statement: Punctuality improved by 50 percent; no baseline or absolute rate published

gaps.model_treatment: Use ten days and the official market index as separately sourced values; do not describe CNY 1130 as Haohang's quote or add an invented booking wait.
Retain 19/23/27 tonnes as an optional public shipper-profile sensitivity; do not call it completed Chongqing-Shanghai order data.
Keep official aggregate mode factors as the comparable baseline; equipment-level road values are sensitivity context only, and no measured train or vessel emissions are claimed.
